title: Amazing convenience and control!
review:
We purchased gohenry for our 12 year old a year ago after reading about it in the Wall Street Journal (May 2019).  We love it!  He keeps the card in a holder on the back of his phone so it is always with him.  He is so proud of it and it has been an incredible convenience and teaching opportunity for us.  

Favorite features:  Just like a paycheck, kids have to wait til the weekly payday to get what they have earned. This and the saving features help kids learn to budget. 
Parents can set both dollar limits for purchases and if purchases can be made online or if cash can be withdrawn. Changes can easily be made from the parent account. We have the online purchases turned off, but can turn them on if we agree on a purchase he wants to make, and then turn it off again.  (Have you ever thought about all the things your kid could purchase online?)

Weekly pay can be a combination of automatic allowance and earned money or one or the other. Some reviewers seem to have missed this.  
You can choose to let the kid check off completed tasks (convenient if you trust them) or you can have it set up so only a parent can check them off. 

Card use can be turned off temporarily and PINs retrieved if forgotten. Purchases will be declined for insufficient funds and the account cannot be overdrawn. All great features for a card in the hands of a child!

Tips: 
There is an easy work-around for there being no daily task option. I set up the daily task (as weekly) seven times and labeled each with the day of the week. Example: ΓÇ£walk dog-Monday, walk dog-TuesdayΓÇ¥. Then he/we check it off for each day it is done. 

Occasionally (although rarely) your child actually needs cash. Fees to withdraw cash from gohenry at our bank ATM were high. Although some retail stores gave the cash back option during checkout (just like any debit card), the transaction would never pay out the cash. Now that money can be transferred backwards from the kidΓÇÖs account to the parentΓÇÖs, we just transfer the money back to us and give him cash. We also encourage him to keep cash he is given for birthdays, etc for these rare occasions. 

Some reviews mention cards sometimes not working at retailers. In a year of use, this has never happened to us.
